ukratko: The big story is a paper showing GPT-6 Astra can read and directly edit another model's "weights". Simon Willison reproduced the trick with Qwen 3.8 27B on a laptop, but says the hype is overblown. For iOS developers, the iOS 27.3 beta matters more today: Siri AI can now act across all apps. Anthropic shipped Message Threads, which speeds up long agent conversations, and FlashProve, which cryptographically proves which model produced an answer.

vesti.naslov: iOS 27.3 beta: Siri AI gets access to third-party apps
vesti.staSeDesilo: In the iOS 27.3 developer preview, Apple lets the new Siri AI features work across all apps. Siri draws on the user's personal context, understands natural language and can see what's on screen. There's also "app skills": developers bundle several steps into a single action, and users don't have to say the app's name for Siri to invoke the skill.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: This is the most directly relevant news for your SwiftUI apps. Developers who add app skills early will have Siri calling them instead of users opening the app. Check Apple's documentation for API details; the article doesn't cover them.

vesti.naslov: "Weight-Space Programming": GPT-6 Astra fixed another model by editing its numbers directly, no training
vesti.staSeDesilo: MIT researchers (Takehi, Teoh, Zhang, Khattab) showed that GPT-6 Astra can read the raw weights of a small model, the numbers that determine how it behaves, and edit them. On Qwen3.5-0.8B, Astra found the cause of the model looping and changed only 0.016% of the weights. The MATH-500 score jumped from 7.9% to 48.1%. On Gemma 3 there was almost no effect. Simon Willison reproduced part of the experiment locally with Qwen 3.8 27B: after 45 to 65 minutes of thinking, the model correctly identified three of four games.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: This is the first concrete example of one model fixing another without classic training, which immediately raises the topic of AI accelerating its own development. So far it only works on small models and simple tasks. Willison says a patient person with pen and paper would probably reach similar conclusions.

vesti.naslov: Claude API: Message Threads sends only new messages, not the whole conversation
vesti.staSeDesilo: Anthropic has released Message Threads in public beta. An agent no longer sends the full conversation history with every request, only what's new. For requests of 500K to 1M tokens, time to first token drops by about 35%. The thread is stored encrypted in memory and expires after five minutes of inactivity.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: If you build long-context agents, responses arrive faster. Token usage and cost stay the same, since Claude still processes the full history. The feature isn't covered by ZDR (zero data retention, a mode where data isn't stored), which matters if you handle sensitive data.

vesti.naslov: Anthropic FlashProve: cryptographic proof that an answer really came from the stated model
vesti.staSeDesilo: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team has released FlashProve, an open research prototype for "provable inference". The system uses a zkSNARK, a cryptographic proof that reveals nothing about the model's weights, to confirm that an answer came from a specific model. On Llama 4 Maverick (400B) it proves about 110 tokens per second on a single H100. The 18.78 MB proof is verified in 17 seconds on an ordinary CPU, but proving costs 70 to 95 times more GPU time than simply running the model.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: Today you can't verify whether an API provider or router is really serving you the expensive model or quietly swapping in a cheaper one. For now this is only a prototype and too expensive for everyday use, but it shows a direction in which the problem could be solved.

vesti.naslov: GPT-6.2 Astra spotted in Codex, release likely near (unconfirmed)
vesti.staSeDesilo: GPT-6.2-Astra has appeared in usage views in Codex. That suggests OpenAI is probably already quietly routing some requests to the new model, as a test or gradual rollout. According to unconfirmed reports, OpenAI skipped 6.1 Astra over concerns about deception. OpenAI hasn't confirmed any of this.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: If you use Codex, you may already be working with the new model without knowing it. If Codex's behavior has changed for you lately, this is a possible explanation.

vesti.naslov: Anthropic's IPO filing: $33 billion in revenue, but $104 billion in losses
vesti.staSeDesilo: In an amended IPO prospectus, Anthropic reports $33.24 billion in revenue for the first nine months of 2026, growth of 1,200%. Net loss for the same period is $104 billion, and compute and infrastructure commitments come to about $895.4 billion. TechCrunch notes that compute margins are getting worse even though they were supposed to improve.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: This helps explain why companies are cutting limits and changing subscriptions these days. Flat-rate AI is more expensive to provide than it looks, so expect terms to keep changing.

vesti.naslov: Apple: dating apps and AI "partners" are 18+ only
vesti.staSeDesilo: Under the new App Store rules, dating apps must carry an 18+ rating. The same applies to AI companions, meaning companionship chatbots, if they offer sexual or romantic content.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: If you're building a chatbot with a "personality" or a dating app, check the age rating before your next review submission. An 18+ rating means losing younger users.

vesti.naslov: Google to schools: opt out of AI, and you lose Search too
vesti.staSeDesilo: For student accounts in primary and secondary schools, Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Google Search will be off by default until an administrator turns them on. However, AI can't be disabled separately: when a school declines AI, it also loses Search, because Google says "search and AI are deeply connected".
vesti.zastoJeBitno: This shows Google no longer treats AI as an add-on but as part of search itself. It's sparking a big debate on Hacker News.

vesti.naslov: Postman reportedly installs AI plugins on its own and tries to send API data
vesti.staSeDesilo: A user reported on GitHub that Postman installs AI plugins without asking, and the plugins then try to share all API data. The report has earned over 1,000 points and 350 comments on Hacker News. For now this is a user report, not a confirmed finding: check the issue to see whether Postman has responded.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: Postman often holds API keys, including ones for Supabase and AI services. Check which plugins you have enabled and whether anything appeared without your knowledge.

vesti.naslov: Kimi K3.1 Pro ships with open weights, but with deliberately weakened offensive capabilities
vesti.staSeDesilo: Ahead of the open-weights release of Kimi K3.1 Pro, scheduled for November 4, Moonshot AI reduced the model's cyberattack capability. In their internal test, this version finds and exploits vulnerabilities in 81% of cases, versus 90.5% for the version without that safeguard. The results haven't been independently verified. Vals has already ranked it first among open models, and Moonshot is taking criticism for unlabeled promotion of the model.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: This is one of the strongest models you can self-host or use through cheap providers. It's also the first time a Chinese lab has publicly discussed safety tuning of an open model before release.

vesti.naslov: OpenAI: GPT-6 Astra designed a device in under a week, from enclosure to firmware
vesti.staSeDesilo: OpenAI's hardware team used GPT-6 Astra to build a device for Codex in under a week: enclosure, circuit board and firmware. It took several rounds of fixes before production, because the model didn't always account for manufacturing tolerances. The company says a newer internal model scores significantly better on its engineering benchmark, but gives no details.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: AI-assisted coding is spreading into the physical world: CAD, board design and simulation. Still, a real product needs iteration and a human who knows how things are manufactured.

vesti.naslov: Croatia's Juraj Bilić elected vice-chair of the Council of Europe's AI and education committee
vesti.staSeDesilo: Juraj Bilić, CARNET's assistant director for artificial intelligence, has been elected vice-chair of the Council of Europe's Committee on Artificial Intelligence and Education.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: The region gains a voice on the body shaping European recommendations for AI in schools. That later influences rules for educational apps too.

novo.opis: An agent in the Claude API sends only new messages instead of the whole history, so the first token in long conversations arrives about 35% faster. Works with most current models, including Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5.

Create a thread, then send only the new turn in each following request; exact fields and sample code are in the docs

novo.naziv: Siri AI and "app skills" in iOS 27.3 beta
novo.opis: Developers can now connect their apps to Siri AI: Siri uses on-screen context and understands natural language, and "app skills" bundle multiple actions into one.
kakoProbati: Install the iOS 27.3 developer beta on a test device (Settings → General → Software Update → Beta Updates)
Download the matching Xcode beta from developer.apple.com
Look up "app skills" and Siri integration in Apple's documentation; check the link for the exact API
Start with one simple action from your app

novo.opis: A CLI for managing git worktrees, built for running multiple AI agents in parallel. Each agent works in its own folder and on its own branch, with no collisions. Currently trending on GitHub.
kakoProbati: `brew install worktrunk && wt config shell install`
`wt switch --create feature-x` creates a branch and worktree and switches you into them; launch Claude Code there
`wt list` shows the state of all worktrees, and `wt merge main` merges the branch and cleans up after itself

novo.naziv: The "which game did this model learn" experiment on your machine
novo.opis: Reproduce part of the Weight-Space Programming paper: you give a local model a small model's weights as text, and it guesses which game that model learned. Simon Willison pulled this off with Qwen 3.8 27B.
kakoProbati: In LM Studio, load Qwen 3.8 27B (Q4_K_M, about 17 GB) and increase the context length, since the default 8192 isn't enough
Take the prompt from the repo github.com/RikiyaT/lm_understand-logs (folder exp1_which_game/runs) and run `LMSTUDIO_TIMEOUT=900 llm -f <raw URL of the prompt> -m lmstudio/qwen/qwen3.8-27b`
Expect 45 to 65 minutes of thinking per game
novo.cena: Free (runs locally, you need a beefy machine)

novo.opis: A speech-to-text API for voice agents, supporting 60+ languages. The model also knows what the agent just said, so it recognizes short user replies better and doesn't pick up the agent's voice as an echo. Speaker and language detection are included in the price.
kakoProbati: Create a Soniox account and get an API key
For streaming use the `stt-rt-v6` model over WebSocket, and for files `stt-async-v6` over REST
Try it on a Serbian recording; check the link to see whether Serbian is among the supported languages
novo.cena: $0.12 per hour for streaming, $0.10 per hour for files

kratkeVesti.naslov: Marvell is buying Lumentum, a maker of data center lasers, for $115 billion in stock, one of the largest tech acquisitions ever.
OpenAI signed four deals in Abu Dhabi (ADNOC, the government, Mubadala, G42), and a UAE investor will reportedly be the largest in a new round of up to $20 billion.
OpenAI released LifeVal, a benchmark of everyday tasks like scheduling and forms: GPT-6 Astra scores 80.6%, but gains only 0.6 points over GPT-5.6.
According to OpenAI, ChatGPT now handles searches equal to 20% of Google's volume, counting only queries that trigger a web search.
OpenAI is merging the Chat and Work tabs in ChatGPT, while Codex stays a separate desktop app.
OpenAI has moved to its own Git backend, Pando, written in Rust and largely built by Codex agents; pushes are about 80% faster on average.
OpenAI quadrupled its bug bounty rewards, now up to $172,000.
Apple Watch gets Siri Recap in the watchOS 27.3 beta, which summarizes conversations the watch hears, and Live Rewind, which transcribes the last 15 seconds of audio.
Netflix is adding an "AI Discover" tab to its TV app, with recommendations by topic and mood that remember what you dislike.
Stanford tested 50 frequently cited claims about LLMs on 20 current models: 44% no longer hold, and a claim "lives" 15.7 months on average.
The SETI Institute has handed control of the Allen Telescope Array and signal analysis to AI agents, so jobs that took weeks now take a few hours.
Nexus Mods, the largest PC game mod site, is introducing mandatory disclosure of whether AI was used to make a mod.
Huawei is telling customers to source HBM memory for its AI chips themselves, effectively sending them to the black market, where prices have risen to about $4,000 apiece.
Fal, a startup that runs AI models for other companies, raised $1.3 billion and doubled its valuation to $16 billion.
Data centers are using old jet engines as generators, because grid connections and new turbines come with years-long waits.
Russian companies plan to move data centers underground after Ukrainian drone strikes on Yandex and Sberbank facilities.
Outside AI agents brought DoorDash only a few hundred orders, negligible next to millions of daily deliveries.
According to Nikkei, the "hidden" AI debt of US tech giants has grown 90% in six months, to $3.2 trillion.
OpenAI hired former US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll as a national security adviser.

istrazivanje.naslov: CoworkOS: a "colleague" agent for long tasks
istrazivanje.objasnjenje: CoworkOS is a framework for agents that work for hours. Strategy planning is separated from execution, and the human and the agent collaborate through shared files (drafts, spreadsheets, documents) instead of chat. From what the agent does, the system continuously generates new data for further training.
istrazivanje.zastoJeZanimljivo: If you build agents yourself, a useful idea here is having the agent and you work on the same document instead of routing everything through messages.

istrazivanje.naslov: CUA-Master: computer-use agents that improve themselves
istrazivanje.objasnjenje: Agents that click around the screen and use programs like a human learn in loops: they try a task in a real environment, get feedback, try again, and successful attempts become new training data. The loops are nested, so the agent improves at several levels at once.
istrazivanje.zastoJeZanimljivo: The code is open and shows how a computer-use agent improves without manual data labeling. This fits today's theme of models improving themselves.

istrazivanje.objasnjenje: A method for generating long video continuously. The model is trained and run so that characters and scene look the same from start to finish while motion stays natural. The goal is for video to be produced as fast as a stream, rather than waiting for the whole clip.
istrazivanje.zastoJeZanimljivo: Fast streamed video opens the door to interactive apps and games where the image is generated as the user watches. The code is publicly available.

ideje.problem: People don't know how much they paid for electricity, Infostan or their phone this month, and opening an app and digging through spreadsheets is a hassle.

Add photo import of payment slips and field extraction via the Claude Haiku 5.5 API
On iOS 27.3 beta, register a "bill status" app skill (see Apple's documentation for details)
Test questions in Serbian and English

A Supabase Edge Function that calls a cheap model (e.g. GPT-5.6 Luna) with an excerpt of the App Store rules in the prompt

Use the cheapest model for picking, e.g. GLM 5.3 Flash via OpenRouter

ideje.naziv: Worktree Dashboard in the Menu Bar

cene: gpt-oss-120b saw the biggest price drop today: from $0.15/$0.6 to $0.026/$0.098 per million tokens (input/output). Llama 3.3 70B fell from $0.2/$0.52 to $0.1/$0.32. Prices rose for Llama 3.1 70B (from $0.4 to $0.72 for both input and output), Gemma 4 26B (from $0.036/$0.108 to $0.067/$0.2) and Kimi K3 output (from $15 to $16). The cheapest in the cheap-and-fast class is GLM 5.3 Flash, at $0.0313/$0.0846. The new GPT-6.1 Terra costs $1/$5, and GPT-6 Astra at $10/$50 is double its predecessor GPT-5.5 ($5/$30) on input.

teme.naslov: Models that read and edit other models' weights
teme.oCemuSePrica: The "Weight-Space Programming" paper, in which GPT-6 Astra works out what a small model learned from its raw numbers and fixes it without training, is the biggest topic of the day. Some see a new step toward AI that improves itself, while others say it's ordinary interpretability, meaning understanding what's inside a model, on very small models.
teme.glasovi: Author Rikiya Takehi posted a thread with the results, and Alex Krentsel independently reproduced the experiment. @giffmana warns that some of the claims are exaggerated. Simon Willison showed that a local Qwen 3.8 27B can do it too, but says a patient person with pen and paper could probably do the same.

teme.naslov: Postman and the AI plugins nobody asked for
teme.oCemuSePrica: A user reported that Postman installs AI plugins on its own that try to share API data. On Hacker News it became one of the most-discussed topics of the day, with over 1,000 points.
teme.glasovi: Most commenters want clear consent before any AI add-on in developer tools. Some are already writing that they're switching to alternatives that keep data local. Check the issue itself for Postman's response.

teme.naslov: Google: no AI, no Search in schools
teme.oCemuSePrica: Schools that turn off Gemini lose Google Search too. The debate is whether this is an honest technical consequence or pressure to accept AI.
teme.glasovi: On Hacker News (over 400 comments), many call it blackmail, while some commenters accept Google's argument that search and AI are now the same product.

teme.naslov: Karpathy built HackerTube in two hours with Opus 5.5
teme.oCemuSePrica: Using Claude Code and Opus 5.5, Karpathy pulled 6,454 videos that people have recommended over the years out of 43 million HN comments, including server setup and publishing, in about two hours. The post drew around 53K reactions and kicked off a debate about which model effort level is smart to use.
teme.glasovi: Karpathy worked at the "Medium" level, so @yuchenj_uw and @swyx are debating whether that's enough for most work. DAIR immediately built a similar version for arXiv papers.

teme.naslov: GDPx: the best model solves only 12% of real business tasks
teme.oCemuSePrica: SemiAnalysis published a benchmark of 206 agentic tasks across 11 domains, from chip design to finance. Opus 5.5 is first at 12%, with Gemini 4 Carbon right behind at 10.9%, at roughly a quarter of the price.
teme.glasovi: @demishassabis welcomed the benchmark, while @dylan522p "apologized to Google" over Carbon's strength. Critics object that the benchmark isn't open, which makes it expensive to verify.
